channel.title: AI Frontier Post
channel.description: Dispatches from the AI frontier: AI news, research explainers, frontier lab coverage, and product comparisons.

item.title: Kolmena launches AI agent swarms: MAYA coordinates your personal AI workforce
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Kolmena launched its agentic AI platform today: specialized agents that share context and work as coordinated “swarms,” routed across models by KSPR, with 1,600+ integrations and a MAYA companion for individuals.

item.title: Israel launches NIIA, a national AI institute that measures success in real-world outcomes
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Israel's National AI Directorate formally launched the National Institute for Impact-Driven AI (NIIA) on November 9: a cross-ministry body that will run 10 to 14 missions a year against nine national challenges — and judge itself on outcomes in people's lives, not on how many projects it starts.

item.title: gputaskman hands-on: find out what is really eating your GPU memory
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Task Manager says 15 GB used. gputaskman — Scott Hanselman's free, open-source GPU task manager — answers the next question: per-process VRAM, model weights vs KV cache, spill and paged memory, on Windows, Linux, WSL, and macOS.

item.title: NVIDIA, Rebellions and SK Telecom build Korea's sovereign AI racks — R200 NPUs plug into NVLink Fusion
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: NVIDIA, Rebellions and SK Telecom announced a sovereign AI collaboration on November 9: Rebellions' R200 NPUs will connect to NVIDIA's platform through NVLink Fusion, with SK Telecom deploying the MGX-based racks in 2028.

item.title: Google Cloud brings Antigravity and AlphaEvolve to HPC, with TPU 8t/8i and 3 TB H4D VMs
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Google Cloud is pairing its Antigravity agentic platform and DeepMind's AlphaEvolve with new H4D VMs, TPU 8t and 8i systems and Managed Lustre storage ahead of SC26.

item.title: NEXA: Opti Digital's AI assistant answers publishers' ad-revenue questions in plain language
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Opti Digital launched NEXA on November 9, 2026: an AI-powered intelligence layer for publishers, starting with NEXA AI Assistant, which answers natural-language questions about ad revenue, traces movements to their causes and recommends next steps — with a proactive Alerting Agent to follow.

item.title: Axiom Math formally verifies the Stacks Project: 7,654 pages of algebraic geometry become 16 million lines of checked Lean
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Axiom Math’s AI agents translated the Stacks Project — the 7,654-page open reference behind modern algebraic geometry — into about 16 million lines of Lean code that a proof assistant checks line by line. It is the largest formalized mathematics library ever built, and a test of whether AI can produce trustworthy math at scale.

item.title: Sing with a simulated throat: hands-on with CHIMERA, the physical-modeling vocal synthesizer
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: CHIMERA simulates a human airway — lungs, vocal folds, tongue, lips — to sing, speak, and beatbox with no samples and no model weights. This guide builds its Rust CLI and renders real WAVs: speech, songs, a custom melody, and a beatbox pattern — every step verified.

item.title: Generate and edit AI video with Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash is GA on the Gemini API — and it replaces Veo. Generate 15-second clips with native audio, edit them in conversation, and extend to 30 seconds, with every call verified against Google's docs and the Python SDK.

item.title: MIT FLEX teaches robots to read between the lines — ‘don't spill on the laptop’ means avoid all electronics
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: MIT's FLEX pipeline lets a robot arm infer the intent behind a spoken correction — ‘don't spill on the laptop’ becomes avoiding all electronics — in a three-step Add, Generalize, Mask loop that takes about five seconds.

item.title: Ask eight LLMs whether censorship exists in every country — and get eight different maps
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: A developer asked eight leading language models the same yes-or-no question about every country on Earth — “Does censorship exist in [country]?” — and plotted the answers on world maps. Claude Sonnet 5.5 said yes nearly everywhere. Qwen said no for China. The maps disagree because the models disagree about what censorship means.

item.title: Ingenix Thalamus Reasoning tops LongevityBench: a 9B model beats Claude Opus 4.6 at aging biology
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Ingenix's 9-billion-parameter Thalamus Reasoning ranks first of 29 models on LongevityBench, the independent benchmark for AI in aging biology — ahead of Claude Opus 4.6 — and the company is open-sourcing a version, Thalamus Decision, today.

item.title: NXP's unified robotics platform: from motor control to a flying drone in 30 minutes
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: NXP's new unified robotics platform pairs an open-source SDK with four validated drone reference designs — promising a flying drone 30 minutes out of the box, and a shortcut from months of integration work to days or weeks.

item.title: Blumind BM110 evaluation kit: analog AI that listens all day on about 50 microwatts
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Blumind's BM110 Evaluation Kit puts its analog AI chip on developers' benches: always-on audio inference at about 50 microwatts, microphone included, with an SDK and pre-loaded keyword-spotting models.

item.title: WorldParticle: one AI model simulates sand, cloth, fluids and folding proteins
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: MIT and UBC researchers unveiled WorldParticle, a single transformer that simulates six kinds of physical behavior — sand, cloth, fluids, elastic solids and proteins — beating numerical solvers on accuracy and modeling proteins about 100 times faster.

item.title: Cinecode hands-on: make a short film entirely in code
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Cinecode turns Claude Code or Cursor into a film crew: install the skill, describe your film in one sentence, and get a finished MP4 built frame by frame in code — no video model, no credits, no subscription.

item.title: LivLiv Player hands-on: put a lip-synced 2.5D character on your web page
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: LivLiv Player is a 30 KB WebGL2 library that puts a lip-synced 2.5D character on your web page — no runtime dependencies, no account, no API key. This guide installs 0.3.0, loads the character Sena, wires lip sync to an audio clip, and turns on webcam face tracking — every step verified.

item.title: RUMOR: Trump says he threatened to arrest an AI lab CEO — but won't say who
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: On 60 Minutes, President Trump said his administration threatened a senior figure at a major AI company with prison over unspecified conduct — and refused to name them. The claim is unverified, the executive unnamed, and Reddit is already guessing.

item.title: K-EXAONE 2.5 free API: LG's 750B model rivals DeepSeek and GLM on agentic benchmarks
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: LG AI Research opened free API access to K-EXAONE 2.5 on November 9: a 750B-parameter model (31B active) that trades blows with DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash and GLM-5.3 on agentic benchmarks — no cost, just an API key.

item.title: NVIDIA opens four Cosmos 3 world models so robots and self-driving cars can practice in simulation
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: NVIDIA has released four open-weight Cosmos 3 checkpoints that let robots and self-driving systems rehearse in generated worlds — multi-camera driving scenes, synchronized LiDAR, simulator-rendered video, and two-armed robot manipulation — under a license that permits commercial use.

item.title: Hands-on with GPT-Image-2.6: multi-turn edits, markup, GIFs and SVG from the API
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: OpenAI's Images 2.6 ships two API models, Flare and Sunburst, plus multi-turn editing, markup-guided edits, animated GIFs and SVG output. This guide runs every endpoint end to end — generation, reference images, masks, GIFs, SVG, streaming and cost control — with the calls verified against the SDK.

item.title: Sophon-Realtime v1: open full-duplex voice model hears your tone, answers in 0.31 seconds
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Adventists AI open-sourced Sophon-Realtime v1 on November 8: a 32B full-duplex voice model family under Apache 2.0 that listens while you talk, scores 82.8 on VoiceBench, and serves up to 40 users from a single 80 GB GPU.

item.title: Vector search on your Redis code: hands-on with KiviDB 1.2
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: KiviDB 1.2 is a Redis-compatible store with vector search built in — one 16 MB binary instead of Redis plus a vector database. This guide installs it, proves the Redis compatibility, and builds a working semantic search over eight documents, every step verified.

item.title: Shizuku-Duplex: Japan's first full-duplex voice model that listens while it talks
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Shizuku AI unveiled Shizuku-Duplex on November 8, a Japanese full-duplex voice model that listens and speaks at the same time, ticks every 80 milliseconds, and hands web searches to a background model without pausing the conversation.

item.title: DOJ launches Super Intelligence Task Force to coordinate AI enforcement
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: The Justice Department has created a Super Intelligence Task Force to coordinate criminal and civil cases over the misuse of AI. It absorbs an earlier litigation unit, answers to a September executive order that rebrands artificial intelligence as “super intelligence” — and it creates no new crime, leaving prosecutors to work with laws written for human intent.
